To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the renal blood flow in a transplanted kidney is reduced after 12 and 16 hr cold ischemia, and that the reduction is most pronounced in the inner cortex, the outer medulla, and the juxtamedulllyary glomeruli.
the renal microcirculation is impaired in a rat kidney model of acute renal failure, and that the degree of impairment is correlated with the duration of ischemia.

in the transplanned rat kidney after 12 hr of cold ischemic time, blood flow in the deep cortex was reduced by 50%, and that the blood flow to the juxtamedullay glomeruli was reduced by 75% five minutes after reperfusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new techniques and the application of these to the study of the microcirculation.
the development of an experimental model of acute renal failure.
the effects of ischemia and subsequent reperfusion of the transplanted kidney.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the renal circulation in this model is severely affected by cold ischemia, with a pronounced reduction in medullary blood flow.
the renal blood flow after 16 hr of ischemia is not completely restored.
the microsphere technique is a useful tool for studying the pathophysiological mechanisms involved in acute renal failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microsphere technique in combination with the silicon rubber compound (microfil) technique allows for a detailed analysis of the intrarenal hemodynamics after renal transplantation in rats.
the microsphere method in combination with Microfil injection is a useful method to study single glomerular and regional blood flow conditions after renal transplantation.
in the transplante rat kidney after 2 hr of cold ischemic, renal function was normal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can now measure the blood flow to single glomeruli, and this is an important advance in the field.
the renal circulation can be studied in detail in the rat kidney after transplantation.
the microsphere technique can be used to investigate single glomerular and regional intrarenal blood flow conditions in transplanted kidneys.
